newsitem.title: USA: CME CATTLE TUMBLE TO LOWER CLOSES ON LIQUIDATION.
newsitem.headline: CME CATTLE TUMBLE TO LOWER CLOSES ON LIQUIDATION.

text.p: Larger-than-expected deliveries against the CME August live cattle contract and long commercial liquidation kept pressure on CME live cattle futures and prices ended near day's lows. Feeder cattle showed spillover weakness but losses were limited by lower corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.700 to 0.150 cent per lb lower with August off most at 65.875 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.325 lower to 0.150 higher with September unchanged at 80.200.
Liquidation by a commercial firm which was a large stopper of deliveries continued to pressure August, as did weaker cash cattle prices this week. Other months followed, traders said.

Selling by ABN Amro Chicogo Corp for Merrill Lynch provided the bulk of selling pressure in August. Lack of demands for deliveries and the heavy amount of deliveries also prompted other longs to exit the market, they said.

Another large decline in boxed beef values and expectations of further weakness in cash cattle added to selling pressure. Fed cattle are expected to trade down $1 per cwt at $64 very soon, they added.

R.J. O'Brien and ADM Investor Services sold August after early pressure from Refco and ABN Amro Chicago Corp. RBH bought August. R.J. O'Brien, E.D.&F. Man and Cargill Investor Services sold October, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures remained influenced by both live cattle and corn futures and eased late when live cattle slipped to new day's lows. Lower corn futures and profit taking on long live cattle/short feeder cattle provided support much of the session, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.04 at $82.27 per cwt.
Dean Witter sold August late after early buying by RBH and locals, traders said. ING bought September early and Refco spread long October/short August at times, pit sources added.

Boneless beef futures ended mixed while trimmings closed firmer in fairly active dealings. Commercials continued to support boneless beef despite lower cash beef prices as expectations held that the CME boneless beef weighted average will hold at current futures levels into the August expiration. The average, quoted Wednesday was $101.51 per cwt.
Beef trimmings futures rose on speculative buying prompted by ideas of stronger cash prices later, traders said.
Refco actively bought October trimmings with Lind-Waldock and Rosenthal Collins also buying, sources said.
Boneless beef closed 1.40 cent per lb lower to 0.50 higher with August off most at 97.20 cents per lb. Trimmings finished 0.50 to 1.20 higher with August up 0.50 and 45.50 cents.
